title: Each tab saves its in-memory list over the shared key, so a second tab silently erases the first tab's recipes
evidence: `recipes` is read once at app.js:3 and never reread; saveRecipes writes the whole list. Driven (T8): two pages in one browser context, add 'A' in one, then 'B' in the other. Stored value was only [B].
failing_case: Recipe Box open in two tabs. The user adds Soup in tab 1, then Pie in tab 2. Soup is gone from storage, and tab 1 still shows it until reload.
remediation: Reload the list from storage immediately before each mutation, or listen to the storage event and re-render. Merge by id when writing.

title: Delete ignores the save result and reports "Deleted" when nothing was saved
evidence: The add handler checks the boolean from saveRecipes (app.js:24-25). The delete handler drops it and always writes the success message at app.js:36. Driven in Chromium (T5): setItem made to throw after one recipe was added, then Delete clicked.
failing_case: Storage is full or blocked, the user deletes "Pie" and sees 'Deleted “Pie”.' The list drops it. localStorage still holds Pie, and after a reload Pie is back.
remediation: Use the boolean from saveRecipes in the delete handler as the add handler does. On failure say that the delete is not saved and will return on reload.

quote: return [];  // storage blocked or corrupt: start empty; app.js tells the user
title: Load failure is silent, the comment's claim is false, and the next save overwrites the stored data
evidence: app.js never reads any load failure (grep for statusEl shows only add/delete messages). loadRecipes returns [] for corrupt JSON and the filter at store.js:7 also drops records without a string name. The first add then writes the shortened list over the old value. Driven (T3): localStorage 'recipes' = '{bad', add 'Pie', stored value became only Pie.
failing_case: Stored value is damaged or in an older shape. The page opens showing 'No recipes yet', the user adds one recipe, and the original data is overwritten with no warning and no backup. Same for any record that lacks a name.
remediation: Have loadRecipes return a result with a warning and keep the raw string under a backup key before any write. Show the warning in the status region on load.

title: parseInt on a number input stores "1e2" (a valid 100) as 1 minute
evidence: A type=number input accepts exponent notation and its validity check passes for 1e2 (index.html:17). parseInt stops at 'e'. Driven (T4): entering 1e2 gave 'Saved “Roast”. Total cooking time: 1 minutes.' and a list row of '1 min'.
failing_case: The user types 1e2 or pastes 1.5e1 in Minutes. The app stores 1 or 1, confirms the save, and shows the wrong time.
remediation: Use Number(value) and require Number.isInteger(minutes) && minutes > 0 && minutes <= 600 so the JS check matches the input's min and max.

title: After Delete the whole list is replaced and keyboard focus falls to the body
evidence: render() sets listEl.innerHTML (app.js:10), which destroys the focused Delete button. Driven (T7): focus a Delete button, press Enter, document.activeElement was BODY.
failing_case: A keyboard user deletes the third of ten recipes and has to tab from the top of the page to reach the next Delete button.
remediation: After delete, move focus to the next row's Delete button, or to the list heading when the list becomes empty.

quote: return Array.isArray(data) ? data.filter((r) => r && typeof r.name === "string") : [];
title: Loaded records are checked for name only; missing or string minutes produce NaN and garbage totals
evidence: totalMinutes (store.js:23) sums r.minutes unchecked and render shows Number(r.minutes). Driven (T1, T1b): stored [{"name":"Soup"}] then add Pie 30 gave 'Total cooking time: NaN minutes' and 'Soup NaN min'. Stored minutes "20" gave 'Total cooking time: 02030 minutes'.
failing_case: Any record from an older version or hand edit with missing or string minutes: the next successful save announces a wrong total ('NaN' or '02030' minutes) as a confirmed save.
remediation: Normalise each record at load: string id, trimmed name, finite positive integer minutes. Drop or repair what fails, and tell the user how many were dropped.

title: A long unbroken recipe name forces sideways scrolling on a phone
evidence: Nothing sets overflow-wrap on li or main. The Name field allows 80 characters (index.html:15). Driven at 390 px (T7): an 80-character name gave documentElement.scrollWidth 1264.
failing_case: A user saves a long single-word name (a URL, say) on a 390 px phone. The page scrolls sideways and the Delete button is off screen.
remediation: Add overflow-wrap: anywhere to #list li, or put the name in a span with min-width: 0.
